subject.title: [Bug]: agents set-identity --workspace does not set the agent's stored workspace, but its success response implies it does

question: Should the public CLI solve existing-agent workspace relocation by adding a dedicated setter/update command, or only clarify that `set-identity --workspace` is a locator?
rationale: Both repairs are plausible, but the choice changes public CLI semantics and JSON output compatibility for a stable CLI/config surface.

options.title: Add Dedicated Setter
options.body: Add `agents set-workspace` or `agents update --workspace` backed by the existing Gateway `agents.update` path, while making `set-identity` output explicitly report locator versus stored workspace.

options.title: Clarify Output Only
options.body: Keep relocation out of the CLI for now and add/rename additive output fields so `set-identity` cannot be read as confirming a workspace update.

options.title: Repurpose Set Identity
options.body: Make `set-identity --workspace` update stored workspace too, accepting compatibility risk against the current locator help text and docs.

recommendation.title: Add Dedicated Setter
recommendation.body: Add `agents set-workspace` or `agents update --workspace` backed by the existing Gateway `agents.update` path, while making `set-identity` output explicitly report locator versus stored workspace.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the public `openclaw agents` CLI contract introduced by the identity helper, not only the lower-level Gateway mutation implementation.
